name: Sparta
type: polis; ancient city; Ancient Greek archaeological site
text: Sparta was a prominent ancient Greek polis in Laconia. In classical antiquity, the state was known as Lacedaemon (Λακεδαίμων, Lakedaímōn), while Sparta referred to its capital, a group of villages in the valley of the Evrotas River in Laconia, in the southeastern Peloponnese. During the 7th century BC, it rose to become the most prominent land military power in the Greek world, a status it retained until its defeat at Leuctra in 371 BC.

depictions.text: {{Location Infobox |name = Sparta |image = Lakonia-Sparta.jpg |state = Greece |rulers = Diarchy |factions = Spartan armyCult of KosmosPeloponnesian League |founded = Lakedaimon mythology |date = 900s BCE |abandoned = 192 BCE Annexed by Achaia |coordinates = 37°04'56.9"N 22°25'24.9"E<ref>Assassin's Creed: Atlas</ref> |landmark = Tomb of Leonidas |flags = |targets = *Pausanias of Sparta Deimos}} Sparta is a town in Lakonia, Greece that was once a prominent polis during the classical period. At its peak, it was a warrior society where all males were trained from childhood to serve throughout their lives in a purely militaristic capacity. This specialization produced some of the greatest warriors of their time, and the martial might of Sparta's soldiers held a legendary prestige across Greece.
